binders: Universally quantify a natural number m, allowing m = 0.
Universally quantify a real matrix A with rows and columns indexed by Fin m.
Existentially choose λ: Fin m → Real, then a basis b of the real vector space Fin m → Real indexed by Fin m.
For these same witnesses, universally quantify a basis index p in the first conjunct.
For these same witnesses, universally quantify a vector q: Fin m → Real in the second conjunct, and assert existence of exactly one coefficient function a: Fin m → Real.
hypotheses: There exist λ₀: Fin m → Real and a Fin m-indexed real basis b₀ of Real^m such that A b₀,p = λ₀(p)b₀,p for every p. This is the complete meaning of LocalDef001 A through LocalDef002.
conclusions: There exist real numbers λ(p) and a real basis (b_p) indexed by Fin m such that A b_p = λ(p)b_p for every p.
For that same chosen basis, every q in Real^m has exactly one real coefficient function a satisfying Σ_{p∈Fin m} a(p)b_p = q.
Explicitly, for each q there is an a satisfying the expansion, and every a′ satisfying the same expansion equals a as a function.
mathematical_definitions: Real^m is represented by the coordinate-function space Fin m → Real with pointwise addition and real scalar multiplication.
A is a function Fin m → Fin m → Real, and (Av)(i) = Σ_{j∈Fin m} A(i,j)v(j).
A basis is an indexed linearly independent spanning family, with a linear coordinate equivalence; evaluating b at p gives b_p.
The eigenvector equation means Σ_{j∈Fin m} A(i,j)b_p(j) = λ(p)b_p(i) for every coordinate i.
The expansion means Σ_{p∈Fin m} a(p)b_p(i) = q(i) for every coordinate i.
The eigenvalue assignment and basis are chosen before q and work for all q; the unique amplitudes may depend on q and the selected basis.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every nonnegative integer m and every real m-by-m matrix A, if A already admits a basis of Real^m consisting of real eigenvectors with real eigenvalues, then there are a real eigenvalue assignment λ and a basis (b_p) satisfying A b_p = λ(p)b_p for every p, such that every real vector q has a unique expansion q = Σ_p a(p)b_p with real coefficients. The selected basis is common to all q, while the unique coefficient function depends on q.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The substantive eigenbasis existence assertion is already contained in the hypothesis. The target adds the unique coordinate expansion property supplied by a basis; it does not derive diagonalizability from a separate structural criterion.
For matrices without a real eigenbasis, the hypothesis is false and the implication imposes no conclusion.
When m = 0, the eigenvector equations are vacuous. The coordinate space has one vector, the basis and coefficient functions are empty, and the expansion is the empty sum.
When an index p exists, b_p is nonzero because it belongs to a basis, even though a separate nonzero condition is not written.
Eigenvalues need not be distinct, ordered, positive, or nonzero. No orthogonality or normalization of the basis is asserted.
Only the amplitudes for each q in the chosen basis are unique. The eigenvalue assignment and basis are not asserted to be unique or canonically chosen.

The statement concerns a fixed finite-dimensional real matrix and arbitrary real vectors. It encodes no parameter dependence, differential equation, evolution, regularity, stability bound, or uniform control of the basis.
